_readme: Hand-curated, source-cited genealogy. Every field below is verifiable against a cited verse.
theographicId  links this person to the bundled Theographic dataset (commentaries.db `entities`),
which supplies birth/death years for the Timeline panel's lifespan ribbons. It is
curated rather than matched by name ON PURPOSE: name matching picks the wrong person
for at least a dozen of these. 'Enoch' and 'Lamech' both exist twice (Cain's line in
Genesis 4 and Seth's line in Genesis 5); 'Noah' also names a daughter of Zelophehad
(Numbers 26:33); 'Nahor' is both Abraham's grandfather and his brother; Matthew's
Eleazar is the 8th of eight Eleazars and his Joseph the 2nd of ten Josephs; and plain
'Jesus' is Jesus called Justus (Colossians 4:11), not Christ. In several of those the
wrong person carries MORE references, so 'most referenced' picks wrongly too.
ageAtHeirBirth the father's age when this line's heir was born (Genesis 5 / 11), which is what Adams'
chart prints beneath its time axis. Taken from the bundled BSB, cross-checked in KJV.
lifespan       total years lived, where scripture states it. Absent where it does not.
dateOverride   corrects a Theographic record that contradicts the cited verse. Used sparingly and
always with a reason; a null year means 'genuinely uncertain', which the Timeline
renders with Adams' own '?' convention rather than inventing a date.

people.name: Adam
people.note: First man; the genealogy in Genesis 5 opens "the book of the generations of Adam".

dateOverride.reason: Theographic gives -3874 to -2692, a 1182-year life. Genesis 5:8 says 912 ("nine hundred and twelve", KJV), so from a -3874 birth the death year is -2962; -2692 looks like a transposition of it.

people.name: Enoch
people.note: "Walked with God: and he was not; for God took him" (Gen 5:24).

people.name: Noah
people.note: Genesis 5:32 gives 500 as Noah's age at fathering "Shem, Ham, and Japheth" as a group, not at Shem's birth specifically -- see Shem's note.

people.name: Shem
people.chainNote: Walking the Genesis 5 ages forward from Adam puts Shem's birth at 4004-1556 = -2448, but Genesis 11:10 fixes it two years later, at -2446: Shem was 100 when Arphaxad was born, and that was "two years after the flood" (flood = -2348, Noah's 600th year). The two-year gap runs through every later patriarch, so the Timeline anchors this half of the line on Genesis 11 rather than extending the Genesis 5 arithmetic.

people.name: Salah
people.note: Not Shelah the son of Judah (Genesis 38:5), who carries the same name.

people.name: Nahor
people.note: Grandfather of Abraham (distinct from Abraham's brother Nahor).

people.name: Perez
people.note: Born to Judah and Tamar.

people.name: Hezron
people.note: Son of Perez (Genesis 46:12), not the Hezron of Reuben's line (Genesis 46:9).

people.name: Salmon
people.note: Married Rahab of Jericho (Matthew 1:5).

people.name: Boaz
people.note: Married Ruth the Moabitess.

people.name: David
people.note: Youngest son of Jesse; became king of Israel (1 Samuel 16-17).

people.name: Solomon
people.note: "David the king begat Solomon of her that had been the wife of Urias" (i.e. Bathsheba).

dateOverride.reason: Theographic records birth -802 and death -844, i.e. a death 42 years before birth. Scripture gives no age for him here, so rather than guess which value is wrong both are dropped and the Timeline marks him uncertain.

people.name: Uzziah
people.note: Matthew's list skips three kings here (Ahaziah, Joash, Amaziah) between Joram and Uzziah, per 1 Kings/2 Chronicles -- a well-known telescoping in this genealogy.

people.name: Manasseh
people.note: King of Judah (2 Kings 20:21), not Manasseh the son of Joseph (Genesis 41:51), who is dated a thousand years earlier.

people.name: Jeconiah
people.note: Carried into Babylonian exile (Matthew 1:11).

people.name: Zerubbabel
people.note: Led the return from exile and rebuilt the temple (Ezra 3).

people.name: Eliakim
people.note: Matthew's Eliakim, not Hezekiah's steward of the same name (2 Kings 18:18).

people.name: Eleazar
people.note: Matthew's Eleazar; the dataset holds eight men of this name, of whom this is the only one referenced in Matthew 1.

people.name: Jacob
people.note: Father of Joseph; not the patriarch Jacob.

people.name: Joseph
people.note: Husband of Mary; Matthew traces Joseph's legal line, not a biological line to Jesus. Not Joseph the son of Jacob (Genesis 30:24).

people.name: Jesus Christ
people.note: "Of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ." Luke 3:23-38 gives a differing line from David to Joseph (through David's son Nathan rather than Solomon) -- a well-known point of harmonization among interpreters, not reproduced here.
